page: Microsoft Azure E4ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Edsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C x86_64 processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a 236 GB local disk and supports Premium Storage. No GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-threaded capabilities, with gzip compression reaching 34.96 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.44 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory write performance are relatively constrained; stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and large-block memory write bandwidth are classified as weak. Passmark CPU and memory scores sit in the average tier, alongside redis SET operations at 7.86 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 8.6 GB/sec. Large language model inference on a 7B model is limited, yielding a poor text generation speed of 5.18 tokens per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E4ds_v7 offers a dense memory allocation relative to its compute footprint, making it a viable option for workloads requiring significant RAM without the overhead of high vCPU counts. The inclusion of a 236 GB local disk and Premium Storage compatibility supports data-intensive operations. This server is best suited for memory-bound applications, single-threaded processing tasks, caching layers, and moderate database operations that benefit from the 32.0 GB memory capacity.
